result.title: Fresh at Decision, Stale at Action: Routing New Information to LLM Decisions Already Made
result.comment: A timestamp theory of LLM decision validity with a decision ledger
result.summary: Freshness shapes an LLM decision at the moment it is made; the action it commits to is latent, carried out later, in a changing world. We therefore introduce a timestamp theory of decision validity and a decision ledger that realises it. Six timestamps define a decision; a freshness ceiling bounds what up-to-date evidence guarantees at action time, placing the remaining risk in information published afterwards. Accuracy then factorises into two capabilities: routing, which delivers that information to affected decisions before their revision deadlines, and temporal judgment, which reads it for the time of action. The ledger is persistent state holding each decision's times, evidence and background knowledge, indexed by watch conditions written at decision time. Controlled decision streams with exact labels confirm four predictions across five LLMs, from 8B to frontier scale: freshness alone yields exactly the accuracy the ceiling predicts; models act on decisive news once it arrives, so accuracy follows routing; the ledger's index sets what routing reaches, and watch conditions reach indirect dependencies at low exposure; and the remaining errors concern when a change takes effect. Freshness makes a decision right when it is made; routing and temporal judgment keep it right when it is carried out.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出决策有效性的时间戳理论与持久化 decision ledger：为每个 LLM 决策记录时间、证据与背景知识，并用决策时刻写入的 watch 条件索引后续新信息，把准确性分解为信息路由与时间判断两种能力，在 8B 到前沿的五个模型上验证四条预测。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「决策时刻 vs 执行时刻」的新鲜度上限，以及按 watch 条件把新证据路由到受影响决策的持久状态索引机制，可能为 LVR 中 latent 推理状态何时失效、何时重新 LOOK 或修订提供可核查的状态失效判定与证据路由线索。
